question: What is the primary purpose of the School Health Programme?

options.A: To regulate commercial food vendors around school gates
options.B: To replace local clinics with school-based hospitals
options.C: To promote and improve the health of school-aged children
options.D: To provide free accommodation for teachers and staff

explanation: The School Health Programme is specifically structured to protect and enhance the physical, mental, and social well-being of students. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why is community involvement considered essential for the success of school health programmes?

options.A: It completely removes the financial burden from the government
options.B: It ensures that health habits taught in school are reinforced at home
options.C: It gives community leaders the legal power to hire and fire teachers
options.D: It stops students from falling sick during examination periods

explanation: When communities are involved, healthy practices do not stop at the school gate but continue inside the family environment. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h1)

question: Which group acts as the most direct bridge between the home and the school?
explanation: The PTA brings parents and teachers together directly to address the welfare and health needs of the students. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h2)

question: What is the primary contribution of local health workers to a school health programme?

options.A: Providing clinical expertise and conducting health screenings
options.B: Drafting the national educational curriculum for science
options.C: Enforcing school discipline and attendance policies
options.D: Building new classroom blocks and administrative offices

explanation: Nurses and community health extension workers bring professional medical knowledge to evaluate student health and manage basic interventions. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h2)

question: What does community resource mobilization primarily aim to fix in under-resourced schools?

options.C: Shortages in basic health and physical infrastructure
options.D: Low scores in national mathematics examinations

explanation: Mobilizing local resources directly targets physical gaps like clean water, toilets, and functional sick bays. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h3)

question: A village school lacks a clean water supply, putting children at risk of waterborne diseases. What is the best community-driven action to take?

options.A: Wait until the national government builds a modern university teaching hospital
options.B: Advise all students to stop drinking water while inside the school premises
options.C: Mobilize local leaders and artisans to sink a borehole or repair water tanks
options.D: Close down the school permanently until international aid arrives

explanation: Local mobilization utilizes community labor and donations to solve immediate health infrastructure challenges practically. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h3)

question: Why is involving local community members in school health campaigns advantageous?

options.A: They possess formal degrees in advanced medical epidemiology
options.B: They receive massive salaries from international health organizations
options.C: They have legal authority to penalize parents who refuse treatment
options.D: They understand local cultural nuances and speak the local language

explanation: Local members communicate health messages in ways that resonate deeply with the community's beliefs and language. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h4)

question: Which health intervention is a community volunteer most likely to assist with during a school health week?

options.A: Administering mass deworming tablets and educating on hygiene
options.B: Performing complex orthopedic surgeries in the school library
options.C: Conducting annual performance appraisals for teaching staff
options.D: Auditing the financial accounts of the school cafeteria

explanation: Community volunteers frequently assist with public health campaigns like mass deworming, vaccination, and basic hygiene promotion. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h4)

question: Which of the following diseases is closely linked to poor environmental sanitation and stagnant water around schools?
explanation: Cholera and other waterborne or vector-borne illnesses thrive when sanitation and drainage around schools are poor. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h5)

question: What is a major misconception regarding school environmental sanitation?

options.A: People believe it is solely the duty of hired school janitors
options.B: People think clean surroundings prevent malaria and cholera
options.C: People assume students should participate in cleaning their classrooms
options.D: People know that clearing bushes keeps dangerous reptiles away

explanation: Many wrongly assume maintenance belongs only to paid staff, overlooking the vital role of community and student participation. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h5)

question: What is the primary negative effect of malnutrition on school-aged children?

options.A: Complete inability to learn any spoken language
options.B: Impaired cognitive development and reduced concentration
options.C: Instant development of chronic cardiovascular disease
options.D: Permanent discoloration of the skin and hair loss

explanation: Poor nutrition directly harms a child's brain development, focus, and ability to perform well academically. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h6)

question: How do local farmers directly support school feeding initiatives?

options.A: By teaching science classes on agricultural botany
options.B: By prescribing nutritional supplements to sick children
options.C: By supplying locally grown, nutritious food produce
options.D: By auditing the financial books of the school canteen

explanation: Local farmers provide fresh food ingredients, ensuring the feeding program is sustainable and utilizes local produce. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of monitoring and evaluation in school-community health partnerships?

options.A: To select which students are permitted to graduate to secondary school
options.B: To increase the school fees paid by parents every single term
options.C: To check if health projects are meeting their goals and maintaining accountability
options.D: To punish teachers who fail to submit their lesson plans on time

explanation: Monitoring and evaluation track project progress, ensure transparency, and verify that health objectives are being met. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h7)

question: Why is transparency in reporting health funds crucial for community partnerships?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any volunteer labor in the school
options.B: It ensures that teachers receive higher bonuses each month
options.C: It prevents the government from inspecting school facilities
options.D: It builds mutual trust and encourages continued community support

explanation: When communities see how resources are used honestly, they remain willing to support and fund future school health projects. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h7)
